title: Frontend's inset on the commodity page drops Design release 1's second sentence, so it never tells a user that a consignment needing no health certificate must still be notified.

finding.frontend: The inset under the heading reads, in full, "Each health certificate requires a separate notification." That is the whole of it — one sentence, defined at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:6 and rendered as a govukInsetText at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/search/search.njk:12-14. Nothing anywhere in the frontend's commodity feature tells a user what to do when a consignment needs no health certificate.
finding.prototype: The inset in the same position reads "A separate notification is required for each health certificate. Consignments that do not require a health certificate must still be notified." (app/views/what-are-you-importing.html:41-44). The second sentence carries an obligation the first does not imply: it closes off the reading that no certificate means no notification.
finding.difference: Replace the inset copy on the commodity page with Design release 1's two sentences, in Design release 1's wording. The first sentence also differs in construction — the frontend puts the certificate first, Design release 1 puts the notification first — so take the whole string rather than appending to what is there. The Welsh file beside it carries the same one-sentence inset and will need the same change (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.cy.js). Nothing has to land first. No control is named because the inset is a paragraph rather than a form control; the whole-page shots of both sides show it in place under the heading.
finding.falsifiedBy: The sentence "Consignments that do not require a health certificate must still be notified", or any statement of that obligation, appearing anywhere in the frontend's live-animals journey.
finding.verification: Read both rendered DOMs (capture/html/frontend/fe-commodity-search.html:119-121 and capture/html/prototype/dr1-what-are-you-importing.html) and both 2x page shots, which show the one-sentence inset against the two-sentence one. Read the cited source at src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/commodities/copy/copy.en.js:6 and app/views/what-are-you-importing.html:41-44. Ran the falsifier: grepped "health certificate" across src/server on the implementation side. CORRECT.
finding.correction: The claim stands and the falsifier does not fire, but one supporting sentence in falsifiedBy was wrong and has been dropped. What was claimed: "The commodity feature's copy file is the only place the frontend states anything about health certificates." What is true: six other copy files mention a health certificate — the additional-details hint "You'll find this on the health certificate.", the origin region-code hint, the place-of-destination hint in the addresses copy, a confirmation bullet, and a document-type label in both the check-answers and documents copy. None of them states the obligation the finding is about, so the finding itself is unaffected; the falsifier now reads as the search it actually is. Two citations were also a line out on the requirements side — the inset is built at app/views/what-are-you-importing.html:41-44, not :42-45 — and both the prose and the evidence path now say so.
